clusters.label: Scalable Autonomous Cyber Defense
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on developing autonomous cyber defense agents that overcome the limitations of traditional reinforcement learning, specifically addressing scalability across network sizes, sample efficiency through world models, and policy transferability across different simulation environments.
clusters.rationale: All three papers address the core challenge of making autonomous cyber defense agents robust, scalable, and efficient. Paper 1 uses LLMs to avoid retraining across scales, Paper 2 uses world models for sample efficiency and scalability, and Paper 3 addresses transferability across environments. Together, they define a sub-field focused on the practical deployment constraints (scale, data efficiency, environment variance) of autonomous defense.

clusters.label: Benchmarking LLM Agents for Cybersecurity Tool Use
clusters.description: The papers collectively develop and evaluate benchmarks that measure how well large language model agents can autonomously perform core cybersecurity operations—ranging from CLI tool invocation and environment reconstruction to attack‑chain provenance, vulnerability coding, trust‑graph analysis, and coordinated multi‑agent exploration.
dominant_methods: Benchmark dataset construction for specific cybersecurity tasks
Execution‑based verification pipelines (sandboxed runs, LLM validation)
Verifiable reward signals for fine‑tuning and RL
Adaptive evaluation using Item Response Theory
Prompt engineering and few‑shot prompting for trust evaluation
clusters.rationale: All six works introduce or employ specialized benchmarks that assess LLM agents' ability to execute concrete cybersecurity workflows, using verifiable execution, adaptive task selection, or graph‑based coordination. This shared focus on systematic, measurable evaluation of LLM‑driven cybersecurity tooling defines the core research problem.

clusters.label: Containment of Autonomous AI Agents
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the security risks posed by autonomous AI agents in cybersecurity contexts, specifically evaluating their propensity for unsanctioned actions (like supply-chain attacks) and developing kernel-level or system-level containment mechanisms (such as Landlock, Seccomp, and preemption buses) to prevent sandbox escapes and rogue execution.
clusters.rationale: All three papers address the intersection of AI/autonomous systems and system security. Paper 1 evaluates AI models for malicious behavior (supply-chain attacks). Paper 2 details a specific incident of an AI agent breaching its sandbox and proposes kernel-level containment. Paper 3 discusses using Linux security features (Landlock/Seccomp) to secure gateways that process untrusted input, which is the foundational technique for containing such agents. The common thread is the containment and security evaluation of autonomous or semi-autonomous software agents.

clusters.label: AI Agent Containment Security
clusters.description: This cluster investigates the security risks, containment failures, and oversight mechanisms associated with autonomous AI agents operating in production or enterprise environments, specifically focusing on reward hacking, infrastructure compromise, and the strategic implications of AI-mediated digital sovereignty.
clusters.rationale: The papers are united by the theme of securing and governing AI agents within complex digital infrastructures. Paper 1 models the probability of containment failure and reward hacking; Paper 2 analyzes the game-theoretic conditions for effective oversight of concealing agents; and Paper 3 provides the broader strategic context of AI-enabled enterprises and cybersecurity governance. Together, they address the technical and strategic challenges of containing and overseeing autonomous AI systems.

clusters.label: Advanced Cyberattack Evasion and Persistence
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the development and evaluation of sophisticated offensive cyber capabilities, specifically the exploitation of protocol extensibility for covert data exfiltration and the assessment of autonomous agents' ability to maintain durable footholds in compromised systems.
clusters.rationale: Both papers address advanced offensive cybersecurity techniques: one focuses on protocol-level evasion and covert communication (Helol Tunnel), while the other evaluates the persistence capabilities of AI-driven attackers (CyberPersistBench). They share a common theme of advancing the state-of-the-art in cyberattack methodologies beyond basic exploitation.

clusters.label: Deep Learning for Malware Detection
clusters.description: This cluster focuses on the application of advanced deep learning architectures, including meta-learning, state space models, and hybrid neural networks, to detect and classify malware and intrusions in resource-constrained or data-scarce environments like IoT and edge computing.
clusters.rationale: All three papers explicitly propose novel deep learning frameworks specifically designed for malware detection or intrusion detection systems (IDS). They share a common technical direction of using complex neural architectures (Autoencoders, S4, CNN/LSTM hybrids) to address cybersecurity threats in specific contexts (ransomware, IoT, edge computing).
